newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-April 15.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-April 15.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Tuesday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:
** The Congress party, riven with sharp divisions over the toppling of Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's government last week, offers to back any new candidate of the ousted coalition for the top job
** Former Congress minister Pranab Mukherjee says the Congress would withdraw the claim made by party president Sitaram Kesri to form a new government, after the United Front elects a new leader
Asked how long Congress support to a new government would last, Mukherjee says: "It will depend on their performance"
** The centre-left coalition prepares to change leader after the Congress agrees to resume support, but some alliance members are uneasy over renewed power-sharing deal

** Parliament has agreed to take up the nation's pathbreaking 1997/98 (April-March) federal budget next week, but it is unclear if the political crisis and amendments will blunt its thrust, polticians say
"Most probably amendments will come from various parties, some consensus will come," Congress party spokesman Vithal Gadgil tells Reuters

** Bankers expect a cut in the maximum interest rate set by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on term deposits with maturity above 30 days and up to one year in the central bank's monetary and credit policy for the first half of 1997/98 due to be announced later today
Some expect a cut in the interest rate cap to nine per cent per annum from 10.0. Many bankers expect the RBI to announce a removal of cash reserve ratio on interbank liabilities
** While mobilisation of funds through public issues of equity was poor in 1996/97 (April-March), rights issues fared much worse, according to a research firm

Only 130 companies tapped the market for 272.4 billion rupees in 1996/97 against 291 issues for 652 billion the previous year, says Prithvi Haldea, managing director of Prime, the country's premier data base on the primary capital market
MARKETS
** Indian stock markets were closed on Monday for a holiday commemorating the birth of Babasaheb Ambedkar Jayanti, a founder of the Indian constitution
The markets held special trading sessions on Saturday due to the ongoing political crisis
The Bombay Stock Exchange's benchmark index closed down 44.01 points, or 1.21 percent, at 3,589.72
The National index fell 10.15 points to 1,003.25
Delhi's index fell 8.69 points to 735.05
Madras fell 21.18 to 3,470.82
Calcutta last closed down 0.82 points at 99.75
-- Bombay Newsroom, +91-22 265 9000
